status_summary: No order or law compelling closure of Confucius Institutes was found. A Defense Department final rule published and effective 2025-08-25 (90 FR 41492), implementing statutory limits from the FY2021 and FY2024 defense laws, bars DoD contracts with institutions that host a Confucius Institute unless waived; the waiver authority ended 2026-10-01, and the rule stated that no waivers had been issued as of its publication. H.R. 881, which would bar institutions with Confucius Institute ties from DHS funds, was reported by the House Homeland Security Committee on 2025-05-05, passed the House 266 to 153 on 2025-05-07 and was referred to a Senate committee on 2025-05-08. Executive Order 14282 (signed 2025-04-23) strengthens foreign gift reporting at universities but does not name Confucius Institutes.

timeline.event: H.R. 881, the DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act, is introduced; it would bar institutions with Confucius Institute ties from DHS funds until the ties end.

Executive Order 14282, Transparency Regarding Foreign Influence at American Universities, is signed (published 2025-04-28); it directs stronger section 117 foreign gift disclosure, audits and enforcement and does not name Confucius Institutes.
The House Homeland Security Committee reported H.R. 881 as amended (H. Rept. 119-87), and it was placed on the Union Calendar.
The House passes H.R. 881 by 266 to 153 (Roll Call No. 120).
H.R. 881 is received in the Senate and referred to the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee after House passage.

The Defense Department publishes and makes effective a DFARS final rule implementing sections 1044 and 1045 of the FY2024 NDAA: DoD may not contract with an institution of higher education that hosts a Confucius Institute (now defined to include programs funded directly or indirectly by the PRC government) unless it holds a waiver; waiver authority ends 2026-10-01 and DoD says it has issued none.

title: Compel the closure of all Confucius Institutes in the United States
uncertainties: The DFARS rule finalizes a 2023 interim rule required by pre-period statutes, so it is a funding condition carried out under existing law, not a closure mandate. The only count of remaining institutes found (10 open and 111 closed or closing) dates from June 2023 and comes from an advocacy group, so it is a lead and not a current figure. Education Department section 117 enforcement against particular universities was not searched. Searches performed: two web searches, Federal Register API queries for Confucius Institute documents since 2025-01-20 (three results, including a Pell rule noting a Confucius Institute is not an eligible institution), and the BILLSTATUS record for H.R. 881.
